description:
A guard that refuses to run names the condition it detected, so a reader repairs the right thing.

## Background

The stale-binary guard refuses to run a gate when the installed binary's provenance does not match the tree under review. When the working tree is merely dirty in a build-input path, its message reports the same commit on both sides — "built from commit X, but the repository's current HEAD is X" — and names no dirty file.

The guard's decision is correct: a dirty build input invalidates the provenance. Only the explanation is wrong, and it reads as a contradiction, which sends a reader looking for a commit mismatch that does not exist.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A refusal caused by uncommitted build inputs names that cause and the paths responsible, and does not present two equal commits as a mismatch.
- [hard] REQ-02: A refusal caused by a genuine commit mismatch still reports both commits.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test covers both refusal causes and asserts that each message names its own cause.
title: Make the staleness refusal name the condition it detected
